Generating the Client

The Prisma Client is generated code, not a hand-written library — regenerated from schema.prisma every time it changes.

@prisma/client, installed back in Figure 2.3, is unusual as npm packages go: what it actually exports is regenerated on your machine from schema.prisma, not fixed code the package ships with. npx prisma generate reads the schema and writes a client matching exactly the models and relations you defined — every model in schema.prisma gets its own query methods on the generated client, named after it.

You'll rarely type npx prisma generate yourself, because two things already trigger it automatically: the "postinstall": "prisma generate" script from Figure 2.3 runs it after every npm install, and prisma migrate dev (migrations topic) regenerates it too, every time it applies a migration — which is why the migration output a couple of topics ago briefly showed a "Running generate..." line without further explanation at the time. Either way, the practical rule is simple: change schema.prisma, and the client gets regenerated to match before you'd ever get a chance to call a method that no longer exists.
